elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 14 requires "comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)" but does not state the limit is per occurrence; the temporal/limit basis anchor required by the element is absent and the redline does not add it.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate limit appears anywhere in Section 14 or in the inserted sentence; only a single USD 1,000,000 CGL figure is stated.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained language sets E&O at "at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the preferred USD 2,000,000; the redline leaves this figure unchanged.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Contractor obtains Company documents, data and records and may access Company systems, so the condition applies; the inserted sentence provides only "cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", short of USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance ... evidencing the above coverage".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14: "professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)".

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Contractor shall also maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)."

reasons: Fallback is complete: the retained E&O limit of USD 1,000,000 satisfies the first fallback element and the single inserted sentence supplies the missing cyber/privacy limit at exactly USD 2,000,000, neither under- nor over-shooting the threshold.

Preferred is not complete for four reasons the drafter would have to repair if aiming higher: (i) the CGL limit is not expressed as "per occurrence"; (ii) no USD 2,000,000 aggregate limit is stated; (iii) E&O remains at USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000; and (iv) cyber cover is USD 2,000,000 rather than the USD 5,000,000 required where Customer Data is processed. Workers' compensation and certificates-on-request are already met.

Minimality holds: the edit is one added sentence confined to the single unmet fallback element. It adds no at-own-expense wording, no one-year survival tail, no notice or additional-insured procedures, and deletes nothing from the favourable retained text (workers' comp, CGL, E&O, certificates, material-change notice all survive intact).

Intent is preserved: the new sentence sits alongside, and does not contradict, the existing coverage list; the existing certificates provision refers to "the above coverage" and now naturally captures the new line without any dangling term or cross-reference.

Optional tightening only (not a defect for scoring): the inserted sentence relies on "also" to inherit the opening "Throughout the term of this Agreement" duration. If you want the temporal anchor beyond argument, fold the cyber limit into the first sentence's list rather than adding a standalone sentence.
The "deviation" status is correct: before the edit the clause failed the fallback outright on cyber/privacy, so a redline was warranted rather than a compliant-at-fallback note.
